pr_body:
##### Summary

Closes #8921 
This PR is mainly an enabler for upcoming patches on filling the chart gaps in the streaming protocol., but it also fixes some bugs in the streaming component:
* Incorrect handling of return codes
* Uses circular buffer for transmission to avoid starvation on high-latency link
* Remove the warnings from the time defines that were shown for every file on the mac.
* Restructured the sender.
* Made the locking around the sender buffer consistent.
* Fix a case where the stream version was not negotiated correctly.
* Adds bi-directional comms on the streaming and a place-holder command processor in the sender code for later.

##### Component Name
streaming

##### Test Plan

* Tested configurations of masters / slaves / proxies in docker containers.
* Tested bare-metal master-slave over WAN connection
* Checked the hi-throughput and a low-thoughput scenario
* Cable pulls, gdb pause/resume.
* Coverity scan
* Valgrind

##### Additional Information

Note for reviewers: no need to check the files under `build_external/`, they are only to set up testing scenarios in docker.

Another note: the concurrency has been improved but it is not quite right yet - I will change the thread cancellation / shutdown of the sender to make it more robust across the following PRs.
pr_comments:
Manage this branch in Squash

Test this branch here: https://amossgaps-czdb7.squash.io

This pull request **introduces 4 alerts** when merging 951e0b9eec2eaf54170a28e328530ddd6adc37f9 into 23beda7785ead8e564a9096216c3350fe3dfdd23 - [view on LGTM.com](https://lgtm.com/projects/g/netdata/netdata/rev/pr-61593767dac3c56b34fb0bbfa688bf52d19cecaf)

**new alerts:**

* 3 for Comparison result is always the same
* 1 for Ambiguously signed bit\-field member

Coverity has detected a bug that currently exists in master but cannot be triggered. Moving around the code in the `rrdpush` file has allowed the analyser to detect the problem. This will probably generate a Coverity report when this is merged, but the bug cannot be triggered in the agent currently and I will change the locking / thread spawning in the next PR to fix it.

While I was executing tests there was a test that called my attention, I decided to test the slave using `ram` as `memory mode`. In this situation it is not possible to fill the gaps, but we are not giving any information for our users about this. Should we at least give an additional information for our users on situations like this?

I used the following scenario and I detected a possible bug:

1 - I used bare metal to test
2 - The slave is 10 years old laptop with a wireless 100 megabits
3 - The master is newer, but it was also using wireless.
4 - I started the slave and I let it running few minutes before to start master
5 - I started the master

And I have these charts for the slave:

![err67](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/49162938/83212363-eafa1380-a14e-11ea-9bd1-703ccc370bfc.png)

I observed that in this scenario the first data that I have stored for the master happened at 1:40:24 while the first data for slave was stored 1:40:16, but the difference of time between the Slave start and the master start was 11 minutes.

Another problem visible on this image , it is the fact that the gaps are present.

This looks like expected behaviour:
* We store data on the master using the master's clock to decide when the data was received.
* The gap-filling is not implemented yet.

This PR is an enabler that changes the structure of the sender:
* The buffer will no longer starve on a high-latency / high-bandwidth connection with bursty behaviour.

issue_context.title: Update streaming protocol
issue_context.body:
* Add a new version of the streaming protocol and version negotiation.
* Change the polling code in the sender / receiver to look for messages in the other direction.
* Add a simple state machine in the protocol start phase where the replication will occur

Note: this will happen on a feature-branch so that we don't leak versions with the new protocol version into the wild otherwise they will break when they connect to completed agents.
